Consider the finite region bounded by the curves [MATH: x=2-y^2,] [MATH: x=y,] and the [MATH: x]-axis, as shown below. Using the shell method, find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated [MATH: 2\pi] radians about the [MATH: x]-axis.

[IMG: /graphics/e54f23ad906170b0f9f26e8b54e8616f]

sections.normalized_html:
First, let [MATH: f(y)=2-y^2] and [MATH: g(y)=y.]

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for [MATH: y\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: f(y)|= g(y); 2 − y^{2}|= y; y^{2} + y − 2|= 0; (y + 2)(y − 1)|= 0; y|= − 2, 1]

The solution corresponding to our region is [MATH: y=1.] So, we need to integrate from [MATH: y=0] to [MATH: y=1.]

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the left function [MATH: x=g(y)=y,] and

  • leaves through the right function [MATH: x=f(y)=2-y^2.]

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

[MATH: V|= 2π∫_{c}^{d}y([right] − [left])dy; = 2π∫_{0}^{1}y([2 − y^{2}] − [y])dy; = 2π∫_{0}^{1}y(2 − y − y^{2})dy]

  • leaves through the right function [MATH: x=f(y)=3y-y^2.]

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

[MATH: V|= 2π∫_{c}^{d}y([right] − [left])dy; = 2π∫_{0}^{2}y([3y − y^{2}] − [y])dy; = 2π∫_{0}^{2}y(2y − y^{2})dy; = 2π∫_{0}^{2}(2y^{2} − y^{3})dy; = 2π(2∫_{0}^{2}y^{2}dy − ∫_{0}^{2}y^{3}dy); = 2π(2 ⋅ (y^{3})/(3)|_{0}^{2} − (y^{4})/(4)|_{0}^{2}); = 2π(2((8)/(3) − 0) − ((16)/(4) − 0)); = 2π((16)/(3) − 4); = (8π)/(3)]
